newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian MP wants to rid country of cats.
newsitem.headline: Australian MP wants to rid country of cats.

text.p: The Australian parliament was urged on Thursday to draw up a programme to eradicate the more than 20 million cats in the country by the year 2020.

The call, from government member of parliament Richard Evans, comes the week after a virus was released into the wilds to try to kill around 150 million rabbits blamed for widespread environmental damage.
Evans told parliament that cats, not native to Australia, can easily turn wild and decimate indigenous wildlife.
"I am calling today for the total eradication of cats in Australia," he said.
Evans said he was making the plea because cats, believed to have been introduced on British convict ships and by Asian merchants, were the most destructive of non-native species.
Wildlife experts say there are as many as 18 million feral cats in Australia and about three million others kept as pets.
"I have family who are cat owners and I'm sure there are many examples of people who have a great love for cats," Evans said during a debate on Australia's national heritage.
He suggested a programme to neuter all domestic cats over a 10-year period to ensure their gradual eradication. He also proposed limiting cat ownership to two per household and impounding strays.
"Let me make it perfectly clear, the difference between the moggy next door and the feral cat is only one meal, and a hungry moggy can and does kill native animals," Evans told parliament.
